frontier.hypothesis: Class C is now buyable at 175 insns; the open question is whether the ~10 rows of store-reorder collateral can be refunded by a device that makes block_alloc's insn scan meet the reload's pseudo before the t0*4 chain's pseudo while the STORES stay in the target's A,D,C,S order.
frontier.mechanism: qty_compare_1's equal-priority tie-break (local-alloc.c:1681-1683) sorts equal-ratio quantities by qty number, and qty numbers are assigned in block_alloc's insn-scan order (local-alloc.c:1240-1298). The 24-permutation sweep shows the scan position of the STORES is what moves it; 13 builds show address-computation hoists move it only partially (29 -> 20-25). What has NOT been tried is moving the reload's pseudo earlier rather than the chain's later: e.g. spelling the cursor block so the D_800A36A0 re-read is emitted before group A's stores while the cursors themselves stay after them.
frontier.next_probe: On the flipped base with the target's A,D,C,S store order, stage the cursor block's D_800A36A0 re-read into its own named local declared at the top of the outer-loop body (distinct from the existing `base` local so no reload is deleted), then vary its declaration/assignment position across the four store groups. Confirm with a .lreg dump that pseudo 109's scan position has moved ahead of 107's BEFORE scoring, and check build_insns stays 175 (a shared reload would collapse to 174, the s18fx failure mode).

frontier.hypothesis: With class C reachable at 175, the two classes may now be separable: the 12-object's only non-reorder residual is class B's rows 35/36, so a class-B device that was priced as unaffordable while class C also cost 24 rows may now be affordable.
frontier.mechanism: s17 priced every surviving-CODE_LABEL device for class B at >= +18 rows against a 175 == 175 zero-slack budget, and s22 re-measured the same price structure on the plain flip base (B1 +18, C1 +25) where it stacked with the flip's own 24 rows. On the fCADS base the flip's collateral is 0 rows, so the stacking premise no longer holds and the device prices must be re-measured rather than inherited.
frontier.next_probe: Re-run the s20/s22 device x slack cross-product (transform definitions in tmp/grind/func_800770B8/s22/gen_cross.py, devices B1/C1/D/G/E/P/Q) on the fCADS base instead of the plain flip base, and record whether any device's cost is refunded now that the base carries no rotation collateral. Then re-test the class-B raw-result store spellings (s7/s8 forms, which collapsed to 170 insns on the floor base) on fCADS, since the surrounding allocation has changed.

frontier.hypothesis: The 9/176 five-wide-row-index object is one instruction from a second independent route to class C, and that instruction is a constant-fold ordering rather than an allocation decision.
frontier.mechanism: a1 emits `addiu $v0,$v1,106 / addiu $v1,$v1,126 / addu $a3,$a0,$v0 / addu $a1,$a0,$v1` (two base additions) where the target emits `addu $v1,$v1,$v0 / addiu $a3,$v1,0x6A / addiu $a1,$v1,0x7E` (one). GCC folded the 0x6A/0x7E constants into the index before adding the base, which is a combine.c/expand fold decision, not local-alloc. Its rows 40-56 are otherwise byte-exact with the target, including row 56.
frontier.next_probe: Read tmp/grind/func_800770B8/dumps/text1b.combine for the a1 body to name the pass that sinks the base addition past the constant, then look for a spelling that keeps the t0*5 chain visible (which the b1-b6 row-base intermediates destroyed, all returning 5/175) while materialising the row base once — e.g. an s16 row pointer whose two uses are `row[0x35 + a2]` and `row[0x3F + a2]` inside the inner loop rather than two hoisted cursors.

judge_constraints: func_800770B8's honest floor stays 5. Do not respell the t0*4->t0*2 identity detour in any form. The dependence may only be reached if it is FORCED by real program structure -- e.g. group A addressed through a cursor genuinely derived from group C's t0*4 pointer, where the derivation has a truthful semantic reading and emits no instruction the target lacks.
